response.justification: Broad, senior full-stack engineer with genuinely relevant highlights: high-throughput low-latency microservices at Sociomantic/dunnhumby (millions of req/s), current hands-on work on MCP code generators and agentic developer tooling at re:cinq, strong TypeScript/Node depth, and a craftsmanship background (TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based development) that maps well to reviewing and extending AI-generated code. The main gap is the must-have 'strong Python' — Python appears nowhere in the skills or project history, with the polyglot depth concentrated in D, TypeScript, and JS. Distributed-systems depth is real but dates to 2018–2020; recent roles read as product/full-stack rather than large-scale architecture. Staff-level signals for technical strategy, cross-functional stakeholder management, and on-call/incident ownership are implied by titles and community teaching but not evidenced. Worth a screen to test Python fluency and scale/ownership depth before advancing.
strengths: Proven high-throughput, low-latency distributed systems experience (millions of req/s)
Current hands-on agentic/AI tooling work, including MCP code generators
Strong TypeScript/Node.js plus polyglot breadth, TDD/CI/CD craftsmanship, and founder-level ownership
concerns: No evidence of Python anywhere, despite it being a must-have
Staff-level technical strategy and cross-functional stakeholder management are unevidenced
Distributed-systems work is dated; recent roles skew product/full-stack, with no on-call or incident-response detail
